mutations.because: The loopback check is the ONLY thing standing between a mistyped --server and a request to whatever host the operator named. This tool is read-only toward the server by construction — it sends GET, refuses redirects, and will request exactly two paths — but 'read-only' bounds what it may ASK, not where it may ask it, and the one endpoint that carries every other lane's events on a shared machine is the one worth not asking from off-box. `checkServer` returns `url.origin`, so with the host check gone an operator's typo, or a config file pointing at a shared box, is followed without complaint and the tunnel's only property is gone. The protocol check on the line above stays intact, which is why this mutation is narrow: it removes exactly the host half and leaves everything else in place. The test expects exit 2 for two non-loopback hosts and asserts no request was recorded, so it must fail
command: a non-loopback --server is refused before any request is made

mutations.because: The stall timer is the whole reason this tool exists as a liveness check. Without it a lane that dies mid-step leaves a subscription that stays open forever: the server is alive, so nothing errors, the tunnel holds, and the watch reports a working lane for as long as anyone waits. That is the exact condition the row was written against — lane liveness inferred from a log's byte count, which stops growing just as often when a lane is working as when it has died. `arm` is also the ONLY re-arm point, so emptying it removes the timer both at the start of a subscription and after every event for the session, and the `--stall` option becomes a flag that changes nothing. The test drives a fixture carrying heartbeats and another lane's events past the window and expects exit 3; the fixture is closed only after the window, so the watch ends at 1 instead and fails on the exit code rather than on a timeout
command: heartbeats and another session's events do NOT reset it, and it exits 3

mutations.because: `/global/event` carries EVERY instance's events on the machine, so this branch is the whole difference between watching one lane and watching the box. With it gone, another lane's `session.idle` ends the watch at 0 and the orchestrator records a still-running lane as settled — the failure the row names first, and one that is invisible in a wave's own log because the lane did go on working afterwards. It is also what makes the unattributed-error carve-out reachable, so emptying the branch does not merely widen the filter: it removes the only place the filter is applied, and the `forSession` flag it returns becomes vacuous, which is why the stall timer would then re-arm on every heartbeat. The test feeds another lane's idle and tool call ahead of this lane's and asserts the log holds this lane's line alone
command: another lane going idle does not end this lane's watch
